content:
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on the Routing & Tracking team. I bring more than six years of backend experience in Java and Kotlin, building and operating services that depend on reliable APIs, data handling and messaging. I am keen to apply that experience in a role focused mainly on Python; my Python experience so far has been limited to scripts and small Jenkins helpers.

At Tejo Insurance Tech, I designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API for insurance brokers, now supporting 12 partners and around 400,000 quote requests per month. I also resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox and idempotency keys, bringing duplicates from around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. These projects have given me practical experience building dependable, event-driven services with PostgreSQL and Kafka.

I also bring experience with automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes and AWS, along with regular on-call work. During a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024, I helped investigate and address the issue; the incident write-up was praised. Tessel’s emphasis on dependable services, clear technical communication and taking ownership of production systems strongly appeals to me, particularly in a platform that turns carrier events into live shipment visibility.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise and professional cover letter. It is clearly tailored to the Backend Engineer (Python) role, uses credible production metrics, and directly addresses the candidate's transition from Java/Kotlin to Python without overstating Python experience. The examples involving the OpenAPI REST API, Kafka delivery, idempotency, PostgreSQL and production incidents demonstrate reliability-focused engineering. The letter also connects the candidate's experience to Tessel's shipment-visibility platform and operational culture. Its main limitation is that some relevant technical terms are stated broadly rather than explicitly, and the production-incident sentence undersells the candidate's documented ownership.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text structure, standard greeting, readable paragraphs and absence of tables, graphics or unusual formatting are ATS-friendly. The letter contains strong matching keywords including backend, Java, Kotlin, Python, REST API, OpenAPI 3, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, on-call and production services. AI screening probability is high for the comparable-language, REST, database, messaging, cloud and reliability criteria, but somewhat reduced because the letter does not explicitly mention Spring Boot and does not provide evidence for CI/CD, query tuning, schema migrations or observability tooling. These should not be added unless supported by the candidate's original information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's acceptance of Java or Kotlin backend experience as a comparable alternative to Python and honestly states that Python experience is limited to scripts and Jenkins helpers. It strongly matches REST API design, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, AWS, Kubernetes, automated testing, on-call operations, incident investigation and clear technical communication. It also aligns with the culture of dependable production ownership and concise technical communication. Candidate-material gaps are solid evidence of query tuning and schema migrations, hands-on CI/CD experience, observability tooling, logistics or supply-chain knowledge, EDI formats, Terraform implementation and Dutch or French. The letter appropriately does not claim these capabilities.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the second paragraph, change “At Tejo Insurance Tech, I designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API” to “At Tejo Insurance Tech, I designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API in Java and Spring Boot” to expose the supported framework and implementation language more clearly for ATS and technical reviewers.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the third paragraph, change “During a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024, I helped investigate and address the issue” to “During a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024, I investigated and addressed the issue as part of the on-call rota; the incident write-up was praised.” This more accurately reflects the candidate information and presents stronger production ownership without adding unsupported claims.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 3 — In the third paragraph, change “I also bring experience with automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes and AWS” to “I also bring experience with automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes and AWS cloud services, including EKS, S3 and SQS.” These specific AWS terms are supported by the associated CV and improve keyword alignment with the job description.
